title: Frontline Plus vs PetArmor Plus for Dogs 45-88 lbs

brand.product: FRONTLINE Plus for Dogs Flea & Tick Spot Treatment, 45-88 lbs, 6 doses

alternative.product: PetArmor Plus Flea & Tick Spot Treatment for Dogs, 45-88 lbs, 6 doses

summary: PetArmor Plus for Dogs uses the same two actives as Frontline Plus for Dogs, fipronil 9.8% and (S)-methoprene 8.8%, in the same per-weight-band applicator volumes.
evidence: The Frontline Plus for Dogs label (EPA Reg. No. 65331-5, Boehringer Ingelheim/Merial) lists fipronil 9.8% and (S)-methoprene 8.8%. The PetArmor Plus for Dogs label (EPA Reg. No. 2517-134, Sergeant's/PetIQ) lists fipronil 9.80% and (S)-methoprene 8.80%, with the same 2.68 mL applicator for the 45-88 lb band that Frontline uses. Walmart's PetArmor Plus listing also says it has the same active ingredients as Frontline Plus for Dogs.
differences: A different registrant makes it (Sergeant's/PetIQ, EPA Reg. No. 2517-134, not Merial's 65331-5), so inert ingredients and applicator design may differ. Match the dog's weight band. Prices compare a Frontline pack with a PetArmor 6-pack on a per-dose basis.

aspects.brand: Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health USA, EPA Reg. 65331-5 (Frontline Plus for Dogs)
aspects.alternative: Sergeant's Pet Care Products, EPA Reg. 2517-134 (PetArmor Plus for Dogs)

aspects.brand: EPA record: fleas (all stages), 4 tick species incl. deer tick, chewing lice, mites, mosquitoes
aspects.alternative: EPA record: fleas, same tick species incl. deer tick, chewing lice, mites, mosquitoes

why: Both list the same two actives at the same strengths, and the record found the same 2.68 mL applicator for the 45-88 lb band on both labels. The PetArmor has a different registrant, so the inactive ingredients may still differ.

title: Frontline Plus for Cats vs PetArmor Plus for Cats

brand.product: Frontline Plus Flea & Tick Spot Treatment for Cats, 1.5 lbs and over, 6 count

alternative.product: PETARMOR Plus for Cats Over 1.5 lbs, Flea & Tick Prevention, 3 count

summary: PetArmor Plus for Cats has the same actives as Frontline Plus for Cats, fipronil 9.8% and (S)-methoprene 11.8%, in the same 0.50 mL applicator.
evidence: The Frontline Plus for Cats label lists fipronil 9.8% and (S)-methoprene 11.8% in a 0.50 mL applicator. A PetArmor Plus for Cats label lists fipronil 9.8% and (S)-methoprene 11.8% in a 0.50 mL (0.017 fl oz) pipette, and Walmart's listing says it contains the same active ingredients as Frontline Plus for Cats. The PetArmor label I found is an older FidoPharm-era version, so this is rated medium.
differences: The PetArmor label I found was the older FidoPharm version (EPA Reg. No. 86230-3-85495, made in India). Today PetIQ sells PetArmor, and the current registrant may differ. Inert ingredients may also differ. The prices compare a PetSmart 6-pack with a Walmart 3-pack on a per-dose basis.

title: K9 Advantix II vs Advecta 3 for Dogs over 55 lbs

brand.product: K9 Advantix II Flea & Tick Spot Treatment for Dogs, over 55 lbs, 6 doses

alternative.product: Advecta 3 Tick, Flea, and Mosquito Repellent and Treatment for Extra Large Dogs, 4 monthly doses

summary: Advecta 3 uses the same three actives at the same concentrations as K9 Advantix II: imidacloprid 8.8%, permethrin 44% and pyriproxyfen 0.44%.
evidence: K9 Advantix II contains imidacloprid 8.80%, permethrin 44.00% and pyriproxyfen 0.44% (FleaScience summary of the label). The Advecta 3 Large Dog label (EPA Reg. No. 91384-3, TruRx/CAP IM Supply) lists imidacloprid 8.80%, permethrin 44.00% and pyriproxyfen 0.44%, in a 2.5 mL tube that matches Advantix Large. Walmart's Advecta 3 XL listing says it contains the same active ingredients as K9 Advantix II. I verified the label for the Large size only, and the XL pack is assumed to use the same formula at a larger tube volume, so this is rated medium.
differences: I checked the Advecta 3 label for the 21-55 lb size, not the XL pack. A different registrant makes it (TruRx, EPA Reg. No. 91384-3). Both contain permethrin, which is TOXIC TO CATS, so never use either on cats. Walmart warned that its price may be out of date, and the 4-dose Advecta pack is compared with the 6-dose Advantix pack per dose.

aspects.alternative: EPA record: 15 pest groups, same list (fleas, ticks incl. deer tick, mosquitoes, biting flies and lice)

why: Advecta 3 lists the same three actives at the same strengths as K9 Advantix II (imidacloprid 8.8%, permethrin 44%, pyriproxyfen 0.44%), with the same pest targets on the EPA record. The label checked was the 21-55 lb Advecta, not the XL pack, so the match for the XL rests on that label and Walmart's listing.
